<!--
================================================================================
  Figure Panel  : 2Q  (Fig 2P lollipop is also generated in this script)
  Description   : All-vs-all Pearson correlation between batch-corrected
                  metabolomics and RPPA protein expression in matched COLOSSUS
                  samples. Significant pairs (FDR < 0.2) are identified, and
                  the top correlated pairs are visualised as a lollipop plot.
                  A highlighted scatter plot for one specific pair
                  (Hydrocinnamic acid vs PDK-S241 / FAK) is produced for Fig 2Q.
  Input data    : Metabolomics: 20200902_ColossusResults_Metabolomics_...txt
                  RPPA:         20200803_Colossus_RPPA_datasheet_...txt
  Output        : 2P_..._RPPA_correlation_p_values_plot.pdf  (lollipop)
                  2Q_..._PDK_S241_scatter_plot.pdf          (highlighted pair)
  R packages    : ggplot2, ggpubr, reshape2, stringr
  Authors       : Anguraj Sadanandam
  Note          : Update both file paths below before running.
================================================================================
-->

## Step 1 – Load metabolomics data

```{r load-metabolomics}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)
library(reshape2)
library(stringr)

# Load batch-corrected metabolomics matrix (metabolites × samples).
metab <- read.delim(
  "20200902_ColossusResults_Metabolomics_2_tissue_weight_Centre_run_batch_corrected_data.txt",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
dim(metab)

# Remove metabolites without HMDB annotation ("Unknown").
unk         <- grep("Unknown", metab[, 1])
metab_known <- metab[-unk, ]
dim(metab_known)

# Filter to metabolites with SD > 1 (high variability across samples).
sd_metab   <- apply(metab_known[, -1], 1, sd)
w_sd_metab <- which(sd_metab > 1)
metab_known_sd <- metab_known[w_sd_metab, ]
dim(metab_known_sd)
```

## Step 2 – Load RPPA protein expression data

```{r load-rppa}
# Load normalised RPPA data (antibody probes × samples).
rppa <- read.delim(
  "20200803_Colossus_RPPA_datasheet_June15_normalized_data_Jochen.txt",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
dim(rppa)
```

## Step 3 – Match samples and compute all-vs-all correlations

```{r correlations}
# Match sample columns between metabolomics and RPPA matrices.
# Only samples present in both datasets are used.
m <- match(colnames(metab_known_sd), colnames(rppa))
w <- which(!is.na(m))
cat("Matched samples:", length(w), "\n")

# Subset both matrices to matched samples only.
rppa_1          <- cbind(rppa[, 1],          rppa[, m[w]])
metab_known_sd_1 <- cbind(metab_known_sd[, 1], metab_known_sd[, w])

# All-vs-all Pearson correlation: every metabolite × every RPPA protein.
# Results stored in parallel vectors for metabolite name, protein name,
# correlation coefficient, and raw p-value.
corr       <- NULL
p          <- NULL
metab_names <- NULL
exp_names  <- NULL
n <- 1

for (i in 1:nrow(metab_known_sd)) {
  for (j in 1:nrow(rppa_1)) {
    test        <- cor.test(as.numeric(metab_known_sd_1[i, -1]),
                            as.numeric(rppa_1[j, -1]),
                            method = "pearson")
    corr[n]        <- test$estimate
    p[n]           <- test$p.value
    metab_names[n] <- metab_known_sd_1[i, 1]
    exp_names[n]   <- rppa_1[j, 1]
    n <- n + 1
  }
}

# Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction across all tested pairs.
p.adj_1   <- p.adjust(p, method = "fdr")

# Retain only pairs with FDR < 0.2 (stringent threshold given multiple testing).
w_p.adj_1   <- which(p.adj_1 < 0.2)
cat("Significant pairs (FDR < 0.2):", length(w_p.adj_1), "\n")

corr_sig_1   <- corr[w_p.adj_1]
p_sig_1      <- p[w_p.adj_1]
p.adj_sig_1  <- p.adj_1[w_p.adj_1]
metab_names_1 <- metab_names[w_p.adj_1]
exp_names_1   <- exp_names[w_p.adj_1]

corr_all <- cbind(metab_names_1, exp_names_1, corr_sig_1, p_sig_1, p.adj_sig_1)
dim(corr_all)

# Optional: save the full significant correlation table.
# write.table(corr_all,
#   "results/2P_COLOSUSS_known_metabolites_sd1_RPPA_correlation_p_values.txt",
#   row.names = FALSE, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE)
```

## Step 4 – Figure 2P: Lollipop plot of top metabolite–protein pairs

```{r lollipop-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# Convert to data frame and coerce numeric columns.
plot_df <- as.data.frame(corr_all, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
plot_df$corr_sig_1  <- as.numeric(plot_df$corr_sig_1)
plot_df$p.adj_sig_1 <- as.numeric(plot_df$p.adj_sig_1)

# Keep only positively correlated pairs (relevant for this figure).
plot_df <- plot_df[!is.na(plot_df$corr_sig_1) &
                   !is.na(plot_df$p.adj_sig_1) &
                   plot_df$corr_sig_1 > 0, ]

# Select top 15 pairs ranked by Pearson r (strongest positive first).
plot_df <- plot_df[order(-plot_df$corr_sig_1), ]
plot_df <- plot_df[1:min(15, nrow(plot_df)), ]

# Shorten long metabolite names for display; strip mass/RT suffix (_mz_rt).
name_map <- c(
  "2-[(2S,4aR,8aS)-2-Hydroxy-4a-methyl-8-methylenedecahydro-2-naphthalenyl]acrylic acid_250.16_1.66" = "HMMNA"
)
plot_df$metab_clean <- ifelse(
  plot_df$metab_names_1 %in% names(name_map),
  name_map[plot_df$metab_names_1],
  sub("_[0-9.]+_[0-9.]+$", "", plot_df$metab_names_1)
)

# Create combined metabolite / protein pair label, wrapped for readability.
plot_df$pair_label <- str_wrap(
  paste(plot_df$metab_clean, "/", plot_df$exp_names_1),
  width = 40
)

# Sort ascending so lowest correlation is at the bottom of the y-axis.
plot_df <- plot_df[order(plot_df$corr_sig_1), ]
plot_df$pair_id <- seq_len(nrow(plot_df))

# Lollipop plot: x = Pearson r, y = metabolite/protein pair.
# Dot colour encodes –log10(FDR) — darker = more significant.
p_lollipop <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = corr_sig_1, y = pair_id)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = corr_sig_1, yend = pair_id),
               linewidth = 0.4, colour = "black") +
  geom_point(aes(fill = -log10(pmax(p.adj_sig_1, 1e-300))),
             shape = 21, size = 4, colour = "black", stroke = 0.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = plot_df$pair_id, labels = plot_df$pair_label) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "-log10(adj p-value)", direction = 1) +
  labs(x = "Pearson correlation coefficient", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text.x        = element_text(size = 12),
        plot.margin        = margin(t = 10, r = 40, b = 10, l = 10))

# Save to PDF (Figure 2P).
ggsave(
  "results/2P_20260427_COLOSUSS_known_metabolites_sd1_RPPA_correlation_p_values_plot.pdf",
  plot  = p_lollipop,
  width = 10, height = 8, units = "in", device = cairo_pdf
)
print(p_lollipop)
```

## Step 5 – Figure 2Q: Highlighted scatter for one specific pair

```{r scatter-highlighted, fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
# Spot-check: verify the row index for the metabolite of interest.
# Example: Hydrocinnamic acid (row 181 in metab_known after SD filter).
grep("Heptadecanoic acid", metab_known[, 1])  # confirm index

# Extract the specific metabolite and RPPA protein of interest.
# Row 181 = selected metabolite; row 24 = PDK-S241 in rppa_1.
df_scatter <- data.frame(
  Metabolite = as.numeric(metab_known[181, w]),
  FAKp       = as.numeric(rppa_1[24, -1])
)
colnames(df_scatter) <- c("Metabolite", "PDK_S241")

# Scatter plot with linear regression and Pearson r annotation — Figure 2Q.
# Uncomment pdf()/dev.off() to save.
# pdf("results/2Q_20240723_COLOSSUS_Hydrocinnamic_acid_PDK_S241_scatter_plot.pdf")
ggplot(df_scatter, aes(x = Metabolite, y = PDK_S241)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  stat_cor(method = "pearson") +
  labs(x = "Hydrocinnamic acid (a.u.)", y = "PDK-S241 (RPPA normalised)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14)
# dev.off()
```
